rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one stepped, compact mass, so it clears the coherence gate and avoids the cross-view collisions that would invalidate it. The dominant gesture is clear: a low bar/plate that terraces upward toward one side. That said, it is still mostly a solid object with very little carved public space, so it under-delivers on the neighborhood_living brief’s active-ground and public-void requirements. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only indirectly; there is no legible court, notch, undercut, or seam that clearly activates that access edge. Program fit is acceptable at a coarse level because the form is low-rise, capacity-aware, and not a tower or large-span hall, but it remains somewhat generic and sealed. The stepped silhouette is coherent rather than arbitrary, so the section is a strength, but the next edit should preserve the dominant stepped bar while carving a clearer public threshold/void aligned to the access edge.
